body:
wade-code-review — Reviewed PR #5015 at `5061623a346ba5e8d22a6de8b3ab4cc058023214` against merge base `61988242460342b26f153ae5e05ec0b294174904`. The required Nix build excludes the new AMX assertions. The inline comment identifies the configuration and verification needed.

Each requested skill was applied separately:

- `ben-review`: no new missing shared abstraction or argument-list finding.
- `wade-code-review`: one test-coverage finding.
- `cpp-coding-guide`: new literal arguments and lane masks need named constants.
- `positron-code-review`: no new temporary review narration.
- `simplify-cpp-comments`: one recommended reduction of the scratch-buffer comment.
- `tron-code-review`: no confirmed production correctness defect in the inspected paths.

Validation: an isolated AVX-512 probe using the production transpose helper and loop passed all 5,184 output and guard positions. It covered 4 and 16 query heads and row strides of 64 and 80 floats. The required GitHub checks are green, subject to the test-coverage finding above. No full Tron build, real AMX execution, FPGA workload, or benchmark reproduction was performed for this review.

PR review: Short version. I checked the six touched files at HEAD 5061623a34 against the PR body (the "How to review this PR" questions and the Verification table), the comment accuracy of the new template code, and which code break each new test assertion detects. The code is correct as far as I can see: the transposing store, the pack loop and the PV padding rows are right for both group sizes. Five findings remain, all wording in the PR body or a test comment: one should-fix (the body says a wrong group size "fails to link", it fails to compile) and four nits. Verdict: approve with nits.

Findings that overlap the earlier review on this PR (CI coverage, lane masks, the P-scratch comment) are not repeated. All findings are inline comments.

ben-review: Short version. I checked the diff (BASE 6198824246 to HEAD 5061623a34) for missing shared abstractions, repeated representation details and argument lists longer than four, reading the full HEAD text of all six touched files. Five nits remain and no defect: two repeated type spellings that an alias would name once, one quantity spelled two ways at one call site, one group-size set encoded a third time in a kernel body, and one test assertion that compares against the wrong concept name. Verdict: approve with nits.

All findings are inline comments.

Wade-code-review: Short version. I ran the 35 Wade-code-review checks (dead symbols, debug switches, comment against code, magic literals, names, silent fallbacks, gated or duplicate tests, PR-body claims and CI lanes) on every touched file at HEAD 5061623a34, the PR body, the two commits and the CI workflow files. Seven findings remain: five inline (a one-letter parameter name, two helpers without a header comment, a redundant `inline`, an unstated 4-head assumption in the QK store branch, one duplicated test round) and two PR-body items below. The CI-coverage gap and the `probe` warning are already in the earlier review on this PR, so they are not repeated here (a reply in that thread adds one remedy). Verdict: approve with nits.

Words used here: kv_mul = query heads per KV head. group_heads = the template parameter carrying kv_mul into the AMX kernels. pr-body.md = the PR description as a GitHub reader sees it, cited by line.

PR-body items (not anchored to a diff line):

- Wade-code-review: pr-body.md:108 and :94 [nit]. The comparator row cites `nightly GitHub Actions run 38999609242 (2026-10-17)` without its repository. That run is not in positron-ai/tron (`gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/actions/runs/38999609242` returns 404), and no workflow under .github/workflows at HEAD mentions Glimmer (Glimmer appears only in bin/ci/prime_hf_models.py, bin/ci/test_prime_hf_models.py and config/{models.yaml,test-benchmarks.json,test_model_definitions.py}, none of which is a workflow). The run is positron-ai/systems_test, workflow "System CI (Rinzler 72-core Intel system OCI version)", job system_ci, event schedule. Its performance phase completed at 05:33 UTC. The Glimmer tp4 row is the log line `Running averages: TTFT=3696, TPS=78.69` from root.benchmark_tps (80 samples, TPS sd 0.48, TTFT sd 188 ms). The run's overall conclusion is failure, from the later soak phase (13:11 UTC, "FPGA 2 (99.74 Watts) below minimum threshold (100 Watts)"), unrelated to the perf row. A reader cannot resolve the 78.69 TPS / 3697 ms comparator from the body, and the base arm at :109 reproduces it, so the row matters. Ask: at :94 write "The nightly CI perf phase (positron-ai/systems_test, workflow System CI) runs ...", at :108 link the run with its repository and workflow name, and name the log line or summary the row comes from. The log's final running average prints TTFT 3696 ms while the row says 3697 ms, and the run has no artifacts, so the body should say where 3697 comes from.


- Wade-code-review: pr-body.md:46, :85, :94, :104 [nit]. Two items on line 46. (1) The Verification section names raw-result files a GitHub reader cannot open: :46 `Raw results: rt-results.txt, attn-stats-compare.md, tests.txt and local-obj-compare/ (result set glimmer-20261016)`, :85 `(the rows are in rt-results.txt)`, :94 `summary.md records the harness settings`, :104 `Raw results: perf.json per pass (every request) and summary.md (result set glimci-20261017)`. None is in the repository at HEAD (`git ls-tree -r HEAD` has no rt-results.txt, attn-stats-compare.md, tests.txt, local-obj-compare or glimci-20261017) and none is attached to the PR. Each reference costs the reader a lookup that ends nowhere. Please drop the file names, or replace each with a link a GitHub reader can open, and keep the commit id, the dates and the outcome clauses. Optional: the prefill rows summarised at :85 ("by 0.6 to 8.7 % with FPGA attention, by 1.3 to 14.8 % with CPU attention") have no row in the body. If you want them checkable without the raw file, two prefill columns on the decode table at :73-83 would do it. (2) :46 says the runtron cells ran `on delphi-3bda, our half`. "our half" is a local machine-sharing convention that nothing in the repository or the body defines (plain-English rule: define a term at first use). It does carry a condition: it separates the runtron cells (one socket) from the CI cells on "the whole of delphi-3bda" at :96, which a reader comparing the tp4 rows at :77 and :113 needs. Suggested replacement: "on one socket of delphi-3bda (half of its 8 FPGA cards; the other socket was not used by these runs)". Do not write that the other half was idle unless the raw results record it.

cpp-coding-guide: Short version. I checked the added and modified lines of the six touched files at HEAD 5061623a34 against the guide's Named values and Braces rules. The lane masks, the lane template arguments and the bare `true` at the 16-head call are already in the earlier review on this PR, so they are not repeated here (a reply in that thread adds the uppercase rule for the two constexpr locals). Two nits remain: a bare 16 on a new line that TILE_ROWS_16 already names, and a rewritten fill line that mixes one named step with three bare values. No brace violation. Verdict: approve with nits.

All findings are inline comments.

positron-code-review: Short version. I checked every comment the diff touches in the six files for pull-request narration, review-round references and reviewer labels that do not carry a lasting technical reason. Two nits remain, both comment-only, and neither changes runtime behavior or test coverage, so the verdict for this lens is approve with nits.

All findings are inline comments.

simplify-cpp-comments: Short version. I checked every new or changed comment in the six touched files at HEAD 5061623a34 against the simplify-cpp-comments rules in Check mode (one new fact per comment line, no restated names, types or Notes, call-site comments say only why here). 22 inline comments remain, 4 should-fix and 18 nits, all comment text only and no code change. The P-scratch comment in weights_times_v_128x4 is already in the earlier review on this PR and is not repeated. Verdict: approve with nits.

All findings are inline comments.

tron-code-review: Short version. This reviewer checked the six touched files at HEAD 5061623a34 for execution-path coverage, shape-gate semantics, packed-Q slot ownership across the two instantiated group sizes (GROUP_HEADS_4 and GROUP_HEADS_16, where kv_mul = query heads per KV head), and whether the new tests can fail when the gate changes. Two findings survived verification: one [nit] on a missing just-outside-the-limit gate row, and one [fwiw] on a comment that states a stronger precondition than the kernel needs. Verdict for this reviewer: approve with nits.

All findings are inline comments.
